title: CORS Wildcard + Credentials on All Routes Enables Cross-Origin Credential Theft
description: All backend routes reflect arbitrary attacker-controlled Origin headers verbatim while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This includes the null origin, enabling sandboxed iframe attacks. An attacker can exfiltrate authenticated user JWTs/sessions from any domain.
evidence_safe: OPTIONS /health with Origin: http://evil.com returned access-control-allow-origin: http://evil.com and access-control-allow-credentials: true. Tested on all routes.

title: CORS null Origin Reflection with Credentials Enables Sandboxed Iframe Attack
description: The backend reflects the literal 'null' Origin header with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Browsers send Origin: null from sandboxed iframes (sandbox attribute without allow-same-origin), enabling an attacker to bypass SameSite cookie restrictions via a sandboxed iframe hosted anywhere.
evidence_safe: Origin: null returned access-control-allow-origin: null and access-control-allow-credentials: true, enabling sandboxed iframe exploitation.

title: Auth-Gated SSRF Candidate Endpoints Present (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render)
description: Multiple endpoints that commonly perform server-side URL fetching exist on the backend (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import). All return 401 unauthenticated. If authentication is obtained via CORS exploitation, these endpoints are high-probability SSRF vectors to reach Azure IMDS at 169.254.169.254 and obtain managed identity credentials.
evidence_safe: Endpoints /proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import exist (401 auth-gated). POST /fetch accepts JSON body. These are likely SSRF vectors post-authentication.

title: Technology Stack Disclosure via X-Powered-By: Express Header
description: All responses include X-Powered-By: Express header, confirming Node.js/Express backend. Error pages additionally leak Express internal routing format (e.g., 'Cannot DELETE /health'). This enables targeted selection of framework-specific exploits including prototype pollution and Express-specific request handling quirks.
evidence_safe: HTTP response header x-powered-by: Express present on all responses. Error pages show 'Cannot DELETE /health' format confirming Express routing.

title: Environment Name Disclosed in Unauthenticated /health Endpoint
description: The publicly accessible /health endpoint returns {"status":"ok","env":"production"}, confirming the deployment environment is production. This reduces attacker uncertainty when targeting the highest-privilege environment and confirms live production systems are in scope.
evidence_safe: GET /health returns {"status":"ok","env":"production"} without authentication. Confirms production deployment.
